name: keel
promise: Plan with a critique gate, scope big asks first, send each task to the cheapest model that can do it, and keep sessions affordable.

installBy.note: Everything: skills, agents, hooks, model routing and the cost footer.
Run in your project root. The method only: the plan documents and the rules. No hooks, no model routing, no cost footer.
Run in your project root. The method only. If you already have an AGENTS.md, merge instead of overwriting.

preview.title: An open-ended ask is scoped first
preview.note: Illustrative. 'Redesign the whole site' gets a goal, up to three choice questions and cheap samples before anything is built.
preview.body:
Goal: a calmer, denser catalogue that still reads as trustworthy.

Three questions (choose):
1. Density: [roomy] [balanced] [dense]
2. Keep: [palette] [type] [layout]
3. Direction: [A: ledger table] [B: shelf of covers] [C: workbench]

Samples of A, B and C follow as small static pages. Nothing is built until you pick.

reads: docs/plan/ in your project, for the drift warning and /keel:status
.keel/config.json in your project, for your settings
This session's transcript and its sub-agent transcripts under ~/.claude/projects, for token counts only (the context meter and the footer)
All transcripts under ~/.claude/projects, for token counts and tool names only, when you run /keel:report or its month command
~/.claude/keel.json, if you create it, for your monthly limit
.keel/routing-log.jsonl, for the router's record of which tier passed which kind of task
writes: Nothing on its own. Skills write docs/plan/ and .keel/ files only when you run them
A one-line marker file in your OS temp folder so the drift, context and screenshot reminders show once and not on every turn
~/.claude/keel-month.json: this month's estimated cost per session, only when you set a monthly limit
.keel/routing-log.jsonl when you record a task outcome, and .keel/handoff.md when you run /keel:handoff
access.network: None from the hooks or scripts (a test checks the scripts for network code). The scout and critic agents can search the web when you use them.

limits: Not a pentest and not a model classifier.
Model routing works in Claude Code only; the method and prompts work with any agent.

Keel cannot change your session's model, compact for you, or block a prompt: it reminds the model and tells you. The facts the router uses are the model's judgement; the mapping from them to a tier is code.
The month figure counts sessions on this machine only, at list prices: an estimate, not your invoice.
The security skill wires free scanners and an evidenced checklist; it is not a pentest and does not prove a project is secure.
Cost figures are estimates from list prices, not a bill; subscription users do not pay them. Sub-agent usage is read from Claude Code transcript files, whose format is not a public contract.
